summary: Add user_location table and REST API to support user-scoped location filtering at login
description:
h4. Background

In multi-department hospital deployments, every Login Location in the system is shown to every user at {{/login/location}} regardless of their department or role. This creates a noisy picker and increases the risk of providers selecting the wrong location. There is currently no standard mechanism in OpenMRS to associate a user with a subset of locations.

This was discussed extensively with the community here: [https://talk.openmrs.org/t/role-and-department-based-login-location-filtering-in-o3-looking-for-community-input/49454|https://talk.openmrs.org/t/role-and-department-based-login-location-filtering-in-o3-looking-for-community-input/49454|smart-link] 

h4. 
Proposed Solution

Introduce a minimal *user_location* join table modelled after *user_role* and a user-scoped REST subresource that handles location filtering entirely server-side.

*Data Model*

sql

{code:sql}CREATE TABLE user_location (
  user_location_id INT          NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  user_id          INT          NOT NULL,
  location_id      INT          NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (user_location_id),
  FOREIGN KEY (user_id)      REFERENCES users(user_id),
  FOREIGN KEY (location_id)  REFERENCES location(location_id)
);{code}

Design decisions:

* Minimal schema, no audit columns.
* Leaf locations only — admin UI expands a parent department to its children on assignment;
_user_location_ stores the resolved leaf rows.


*REST API*

{code:javascript}GET    /ws/rest/v1/user/{uuid}/location?tag=Login+Location
POST   /ws/rest/v1/user/{uuid}/location    body: { "location": "<location-uuid>" }
DELETE /ws/rest/v1/user/{uuid}/location/{uuid}{code}

The tag query parameter is intentionally generic so the same endpoint can support future use cases (e.g. encounter location filtering) without schema changes.

*Resolution Logic*
The GET endpoint handles resolution entirely server-side: 

# If the user has entries in user_location, return the intersection of those locations and the locations matching the requested tag 

# If the user has no entries in user_location, return all locations matching the requested tag The caller always receives a usable list. No client-side fallback logic is needed.

{code:none}getLoginLocations(user):
  mappings = SELECT * FROM user_location WHERE user_id = user.id
  if mappings is empty:
    return all locations tagged "Login Location"   // no restriction
  else:
    return intersection of (locations tagged "Login Location") and (mapped locations){code}

*Frontend*

Update useLoginLocations in esm-login-app to replace the existing call:


{noformat}GET /ws/rest/v1/location?tag=Login+Location{noformat}

with the user-scoped endpoint:

{noformat}GET /ws/rest/v1/user/{uuid}/location?tag=Login+Location{noformat}

No fallback logic or dual-endpoint handling is required in the frontend. Deployments that have
not populated user_location receive the same result as today — all Login Location-tagged locations.

Open Questions

* *Bulk write* — is POST /ws/rest/v1/user/{uuid}/location/bulk worth adding for department transfer workflows?
* *Default tag* — should GET without a tag parameter return all mapped locations or default to Login Location?

*Acceptance Criteria*

* user_location table created via Liquibase changeset.
* GET /ws/rest/v1/user/{uuid}/location?tag=Login+Location returns the intersection of
tag-matching and user-mapped locations when the user has entries in user_location.
* GET /ws/rest/v1/user/{uuid}/location?tag=Login+Location returns all tag-matching locations
when the user has no entries in user_location.
* POST and DELETE management endpoints secured by appropriate privilege.
* No behavioral change for deployments that do not populate user_location.
* Unit and integration tests cover: user with mappings, user without mappings, tag filtering.

References

* Frontend ticket - [https://openmrs.atlassian.net/browse/O3-5754|https://openmrs.atlassian.net/browse/O3-5754|smart-link]

comments_before_2026-09-11.author: sbuwule
comments_before_2026-09-11.body:
accrding to me, the work seems to span two repositories:

openmrs-core:

* A new UserLocation.java domain entity (@Entity, @Table(name = "user_location")) with @ManyToOne relationships to both User and Location, plus standard audit columns
* A Liquibase changeSet in liquibase-update-to-latest-3.0.x.xml to create the user_location table
* A new method getLoginLocationsForUser(User user, String locationTag) added to UserService, UserServiceImpl, UserDAO, and HibernateUserDAO
* Registration of the new entity in hibernate.cfg.xml

openmrs-module-webservices.rest:

* A new UserLocationResource.java REST resource exposing GET /ws/rest/v1/user/{uuid}/location which calls the new service method and returns the filtered location list
